title: Mexico’s Ambassador Vasconcelos Says at UN That Ending US Blockade Against Cuba Is Urgent and Imperative
author: Arturo Sánchez Jiménez and Emir Olivares
content:
_This article by[Arturo Sánchez Jiménez and Emir
Olivares](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez%20Jim%C3%A9nez%20y%20Emir%20Olivares)
originally appeared in the [October 28, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/28/politica/urgente-e-
imperativo-poner-fin-al-bloqueo-de-eu-contra-cuba-dice-embajador-vasconcelos-
ante-la-onu), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

Ending the blockade imposed by the United States against Cuba "constitutes
**an urgent necessity and a humanitarian imperative** ," Mexico maintained
this Wednesday before the General Assembly of the United Nations (UN). Héctor
Vasconcelos, Mexico's permanent representative to the body, cited **the
shortage of food and medicine, the lack of bank liquidity and the energy
crisis** as effects that "impact the daily lives of millions of people."

In the debate taking place since yesterday in New York on the need to lift the
economic, commercial and financial blockade against the island, the diplomat
highlighted that Mexico "has maintained its support for the Cuban people
through concrete humanitarian assistance initiatives" and stated that the
sanctions unilaterally imposed by the US against the island constitute "a
structural obstacle to Cuba's economic and social development with direct
consequences for the well-being of its population."

> No people should be forced to face these conditions as a result of
> unilateral coercive measures.
>
> Héctor Vasconcelos, Mexico's Permanent Representative to the UN

Vasconcelos recalled that in the general debate of the 81st session of the
Assembly, Mexico "reaffirmed its solidarity with the people of Cuba and its
rejection of the embargo and of any unilateral economic measure contrary to
the Charter of the United Nations." He also defended the country's "historic
and consistent position," sustained for **more than six decades** , of
condemning the blockade "for considering it contrary to international law and
incompatible with the principles" of that document.

For the Mexican representative, "dialogue, cooperation and respect for
international law must prevail over measures that deepen the hardships of a
population." Advancing in that direction, he added, "would not only benefit
Cuba, but would also contribute to building a more prosperous hemisphere in
solidarity, based on justice, peace and understanding among nations."

"Solidarity must be translated into deeds and not be limited to declarations
of principles," he stated.

> Likewise, he maintained that "the fraternity between our peoples does not
> depend on circumstances or differences."

The diplomat warned that "the use of unilateral measures as a mechanism of
external pressure to influence the internal decisions of a sovereign State is
incompatible with the principles enshrined in the Charter" of the UN "and
contravenes the spirit of peaceful coexistence among nations." In that sense,
he reaffirmed Mexico's rejection "of the imposition of unilateral sanctions
outside the measures adopted by the Security Council."

In his speech, Vasconcelos reiterated "the importance of Cuba being excluded
from the **United States ' list of State sponsors of terrorism**." He
explained that this inclusion "imposes additional barriers on its financial
operations and international commercial exchanges."

"The current situation demands giving priority to channels of dialogue, mutual
understanding and international cooperation," he said.

The representative of Mexico stated that eliminating the obstacles that
prevent Cuba's full participation in the international community "would
contribute to consolidating a multilateral order based on respect for
international law and on the purposes and principles of the Charter of the
United Nations."
